Past analyses of AMZN (most recent first):

[2026-07-31 | AMZN | Overweight | +1.1% | -2.4% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Overweight

**Executive Summary**: Overweight AMZN, but trim the trader's aggression: build toward ~100-110% of a standard AMZN allocation (≈5-6.5% of portfolio if standard is 5-6%), not 125%, in tranches of 30/35/25 with 10% in reserve. Tranche 1 (30%) at or below 271.58; tranche 2 (35%) only into 258-264 and only after a close back above 262.01 or a declining-volume retest — never averaging down into the 239.82-262.01 air pocket; tranche 3 (25%) only on a close above 278.56 on ≥60M shares with the MACD line above zero. Treat 262.01 as a de-risk trigger (trim tranche 1, pause adds) and 246.50 as the hard structural stop on the core. Size so a slippage move to 240-242 through the stop costs no more than 0.5-0.75% of portfolio value. Horizon 3-6 months.

**Investment Thesis**: Direction is decided by the strongest evidence in the debate and is not close. The aggressive analyst's operating case was verified and conceded: Q2-26 revenue $200.6B (+19.6% y/y, accelerating from +16.6%), operating income $27.46B (+43.2%), operating margin 13.69% (+226bp), AWS $42.2B (+37%, fastest in ~18 quarters), advertising +26%, AI cloud and custom silicon each past $25B annualized. The decisive datapoint is the one the conservative never answered: D&A rose 31.3% y/y to $20.0B and margin still expanded 226bp — direct evidence the prior capex vintage is productive. The conservative's objections (TTM FCF ~-$11.6B, debt +93% to $132.2B, interest expense +155%, core EPS ~$2.16 vs $5.75 reported, AR 40.0 vs 36.8 days, $650B of obligations) are legitimate, but they concern balance-sheet presentation and forward hypotheticals, not a broken operating engine; ~$66B of lease-adjusted net debt against ~$105-110B of EBIT at ~20.9x coverage is an over-claiming-fortress problem, not a solvency one. That sets Overweight rather than Hold or Sell.

The conservative, however, wins the entry arithmetic outright and the aggressive never rebutted it: at 271.58 AMZN is 1.24% below the 274.99 range-top close and 2.51% below the 278.56 high against a 9.24% drop to 246.50 — roughly 1:4 reward-to-risk on tranche 1 — and the 246.50 stop sits on the exact cluster (10 EMA 242.70 / 50 SMA 246.63 / VWMA 245.72 / mid-band) where four supports fail together, directly above the unfilled 239.82-262.01 air pocket, so the modeled loss assumes a fill that the gap profile says may not happen. With ATR at $9.51 (3.5% of price), the aggressive's 125% target directly contradicts his own instruction to halve size versus the pre-gap regime: at 7.5% of portfolio a 12% move to the low 240s costs ~0.9% of book, breaching the 0.5-0.75% budget. The neutral's sizing math is correct and governs.

The conservative's own fix is internally inconsistent in a way the neutral correctly diagnoses: 262.01 cannot be a hard stop for tranche 1 while tranche 2 buys 258-264, which is partly below it; and 262.01 is one ATR (~262.07) from spot, i.e. noise-level — precisely the error the 2026-07-24 AMZN Underweight (+15.9% alpha against) recorded when caution was expressed inside one ATR. So 262.01 becomes a de-risk trigger and 246.50 the structural invalidation. The conservative's 20% starter with 40% parked at 258-264 also assumes the pullback arrives and leaves the plan underinvested if 278.56 breaks on volume. The neutral's 30/35/25-with-10%-reserve calibration is adopted, and the 125% target is cut to 100-110% because of the data gaps (no insider data; 32 of 52 news records unsupplied for 07-24 to 07-29; the AWS share-gain claim is vendor headline text while the same set calls MSFT the standout; AOCI composition unverified) and because the conservative is technically right that Trainium raises HBM content per dollar of compute — a hedge on merchant-silicon margin, not on an HBM shortage — making Q3/Q4 memory-cost margin timing a live risk management flagged and the tape ignored. Prior AMZN reflections reinforce the discipline: staged ladders seeded ahead of unfired confirmation gates filled and then stopped (07-20, 07-21), while a pre-event directional short inside one ATR lost badly (07-24); the event here is behind us, so the fix is a smaller, better-conditioned first tranche rather than standing aside.

What changes the call: downgrade to Underweight on any two of AWS below ~32%, gross margin compression attributed to memory/HBM, quarterly capex above ~$55B with FCF negative and lease-adjusted net position down another ~$20B, AR still outgrowing revenue, or a close below 246.50. Upgrade toward Buy on AWS ≥34%, Q3 capex at or below ~$55B with gross margin holding, and a decisive close above 278.56. The $24.4B of Q2 acquisitions and $122.3B mark-to-model equity book are negative-convexity watch items that reverse into GAAP EPS in a private-AI funding downturn.

**Price Target**: 295.0

**Time Horizon**: 3-6 months

REFLECTION:
The directional call was nominally right (AMZN +1.1%) but the alpha was -2.4% versus SPY, so the Overweight underperformed the benchmark — though five days is far too short to judge a 3-6 month thesis keyed to AWS reacceleration and capex productivity. This window supports the operating case only weakly (no evidence either way on AWS ≥34% or memory-cost margin) and undercuts the entry arithmetic: buying tranche 1 at 271.58 into a 1:4 reward-to-risk with a 262.01 de-risk trigger just one ATR away meant the position was likely to be trimmed by noise before the thesis could play out. Next time, when the structural stop sits only ~1 ATR below spot and the risk budget is 0.5-0.75%, either widen the de-risk trigger to a closing basis beyond 1.5 ATR or start smaller than 30% so the entry survives ordinary volatility.

[2026-07-30 | AMZN | Underweight | +15.6% | +12.0% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN — reduce, do not exit, and do not short. Trim roughly 40–50% of any existing position immediately at/near 235.50 (the upper half of the plan's 25–50% band), targeting 50–60% of the caller's normal single-name weight, and place the remainder as limit orders into 236.29 (10EMA) → 240.82 (VWMA) → 242.41–246.38 (Bollinger mid/July pivot to falling 50SMA) so completion does not depend on a rally arriving on schedule. No new long at 235.50 and no averaging down; residual long carries a hard review at 231.06 and exits to flat on a confirmed daily close below 226.13 on expanded volume. Layers that treat 242.41–247.00 as a short entry are optional trim-completion tools only, sized at 0.5–1.0% of account risk with a 248.50 stop; if options are permitted, a defined-risk protective put or collar is the preferred hedge over a linear short. Horizon 1–3 months, re-scored on Q3 evidence of organic growth, capex and AWS segment disclosure.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats and the trader converge on reducing AMZN exposure; the only live disputes are whether this is a trim or an exit, and whether to add a short overlay. On both I side with the trim and against the overlay, but with the trim front-loaded toward the conservative analyst's preferred end of the band.

Why the bear case wins the direction. (1) Revenue acceleration is not proven organic: H1 2026 acquisitions were $39.8B versus $1.7B a year earlier, $24.4B of it in Q2, and the debate contains no acquired-revenue contribution or organic growth figure — the aggressive analyst concedes this "should be reconciled," which is not a basis for full weight. (2) Earnings quality is materially below the headline: of $5.75 EPS, roughly $3.59 comes from a $50.5B non-cash upward revaluation, leaving core EPS near $2.16, while cash taxes were only 3.3% of pre-tax income — a deferred-tax shield tied to the same accounting event, so the "core" number is not clean either. The non-marketable equity balance jumped from $16.2B to $122.3B (11.2% of total assets) on a mark-to-model line that can reverse through the P&L in either direction. (3) The cash-flow and leverage trajectory is the genuine change, and it is one-directional: TTM FCF −$11.6B, Q2 capex $54.2B (+68.4%), capex at 119% of operating cash flow in Q2 and 138% in H1, long-term debt $68.8B → $133.0B, interest expense +154.7% y/y, roughly $67B net debt including leases, current ratio 1.033x and tightening, receivables +30.1% against revenue +19.6%, $650.0B of contractual obligations with $78.1B due inside twelve months, and D&A +31.2% while capex runs +68.4% — a depreciation drag still building. (4) AWS segment revenue and operating income are absent from the materials; inferring AWS health from a 13.7% consolidated margin is not evidence for the single most important swing factor. (5) The tape supports reducing now, not adding: at 235.50 price is below the 10EMA (236.29), VWMA (240.82), Bollinger mid/July pivot (242.41) and falling 50SMA (246.38, declining ~$0.70/session), with only $0.75 — less than one-third of the $7.34 ATR — above the rising 200SMA at 234.75. The report's own arithmetic grades a long here at 0.53:1 to 0.69:1 versus 3–4:1 for selling strength, and the 50/200 spread of ~$11.63 narrows in roughly 16–17 sessions if price merely goes nowhere.

Why not Sell/exit, and why not the short overlay. The bull's offsets are real and were never rebutted: $176.1B of liquidity, operating cash flow +39.6%, operating income +43.2% to $27.5B on a 13.7% margin, marketing +2.5% and G&A −6.0% against 19.6% revenue growth (genuine overhead leverage), record inventory turns, and a tested double bottom at 226.13/226.16 that turned the stock on 101.8M shares (~2.6x average) on 7/30, at the same shelf that turned it on 6/26. That rules out insolvency and rules out paying for a breakdown that has already been rejected twice. The report's own scenario weights (≈50% range repair toward 242, 20% bull escalation above 242.41, 30% bear resumption below 226.13) imply a modestly positive probability-weighted value from spot — that is precisely why this is a partial reduction rather than a flat book. On the overlay, the conservative and neutral analysts have the better of the aggressive seat: a 242.41 short with a 248.50 stop is a new directional bet that only pays if a rally arrives before or after a binary print, misses the gap-down scenario it is supposed to hedge, and is invalidated if AMZN gaps through 247.55. The 3–4:1 payoff is attractive as a limit-order completion tool for an overweight long, not as a core position, and if options are available a protective put or collar is strictly cleaner.

Why the trim is front-loaded rather than staged purely into strength. The neutral analyst's 25–35% now / completion on a rally is the soundest architecture, but the conservative analyst's case for more now is stronger on this specific setup: the 10-Q was accepted ~22:11 ET on 2026-07-30, after the cash close, so the market's first vote on a low-quality headline is still ahead; the volume signal from the 101.8M-share reversal is explicitly unresolved and requires one to three sessions of follow-through that include the earnings reaction; and the 07-22 AMZN reflection already recorded that a 40–50% trim would have beaten a 30% trim when momentum diverged this sharply. Countervailing prior lesson applied: the 07-23 reflection warns against tightening solely on one session's break, so the heavier cut here rests on the multi-week trend decay plus the post-close print and the FCF/debt evidence — not on the single reversal candle.

What would change the call. Upgrade toward Hold/Overweight only on (a) two consecutive daily closes above 242.41 on >60M shares with the MACD histogram turning positive, or (b) Q3 evidence of organic revenue growth ≥18% with acquired contribution separately disclosed, operating margin ≥13.5%, capex ≤$52B, TTM FCF moving toward breakeven, long-term debt flat or declining, and AWS segment reacceleration. Downgrade toward a flat/minimal position on a daily close below 231.06, or on a confirmed break of 226.13 on volume (opens 221–223). Explicit data gaps, not priced either way: no AWS segment revenue or operating income anywhere in the materials, no acquired-versus-organic revenue split, no Q3 capex or revenue guidance, no valuation multiples or consensus, no disclosed mark-to-model assumptions behind the $122.3B asset, no sentiment or insider data, and no portfolio/holdings context — all sizing is therefore expressed as fractions of a caller-defined standard AMZN allocation.

**Price Target**: 228.0

**Time Horizon**: 1-3 months

REFLECTION:
Five days delivered +12.0% alpha against the Underweight (raw +15.6%), so on the directional call this window is a clear miss — though 5 days against a 1–3 month thesis tests only the entry timing, not the capex/debt/FCF argument, which needs Q3 evidence to adjudicate. What it does undercut is the front-loading rationale: I cut harder before the post-close print on the premise that the market's first vote on a low-quality headline was still ahead, and that vote went sharply the other way, while the bullish tell I discounted — the 101.8M-share rejection at 226.13/226.16 on 7/30 — was the higher-information signal. Next time, when a high-volume reversal sits on a rising 200SMA, let the volume shelf outrank the moving-average stack and cap the pre-catalyst trim at the low end of the band until the reaction prints.

[2026-07-29 | AMZN | Underweight | +20.3% | +14.8% | 5d]

DECISION:
**Rating**: Underweight

**Executive Summary**: Underweight AMZN — reduce, do not liquidate. Trim 45–50% of a standard AMZN allocation around the 2026-07-29 close of 226.65 (the middle-high end of the trader's band, per the standing lesson from the 2026-07-22 review that a light trim into sharp momentum divergence underperforms), leaving a 50–55% core; commit no new capital into the 2026-07-30 Q2 print, on which the dataset contains zero information. Do not rely on a 225.55 equity stop — with ATR at 6.89 pts (3.04% of price) and a documented −8.98% gap open on 2026-02-06, express protection through position size or options, not resting stops. Escalate to 25–30% of standard (flat if the risk budget is tight) on a decisive close below 225.55 on volume above ~45M, which opens 221.25 → 219.62 → 213.77 → 209.77; rebuild in two stages only on a reclaim of 230.86–232.82 and then a close above the 200 SMA at 234.66 on volume above ~45M. Horizon 3–6 months, with the event window through 2026-07-30 governing near-term sizing.

**Investment Thesis**: All three risk seats converge on lower exposure; the dispute is only degree, and the degree is settled by which evidence is load-bearing. The Aggressive seat's best contribution is not its directional argument but its procedural one — a pre-committed, trigger-driven trim beats a static full position into a binary print — and on that point he is right, and it is why this is a reduction rather than a hold. But his two load-bearing bullish pillars fail on the merits, and both failures are conceded or unrefuted.

First, the "$569.3B contracted backlog." The fundamentals are explicit that the $569.3B (with $57.1B due inside twelve months) is predominantly AWS compute/power/chip purchase commitments — money Amazon owes on a fixed schedule, not money customers owe Amazon. Relabeling the single largest fixed-cost liability on the balance sheet as demand visibility inverts its sign, and the FCF/leverage argument built on it collapses with it.

Second, "the depreciation wave already arrived because margins expanded anyway." TTM D&A of ~$70.4B against a ~$151.0B TTM capex run-rate means depreciation is running at less than half of capex; Q1 2026 capex of $44.2B (+76.7% y/y) enters the depreciation schedule only when placed in service, quarters from now. D&A +32.8% against revenue +16.6% is therefore a forward squeeze into 2027, not a headwind already absorbed — and it sits inside a stock already being re-rated for spending too much.

What decides the direction is the balance-sheet turn, because it is the actual driver of the multiple: net cash fell from +$63.8B to +$22.1B in a single quarter, long-term debt went $68.8B → $121.9B (nearly doubled), interest expense +47.9% y/y, and capex incurred but not yet paid rose to $27.0B from $16.8B — meaning reported FCF of −$2.5B understates the real drain. The trajectory matters more than the level: FCF +$32.9B → +$7.7B → −$2.5B while capex grows +82% versus OCF +28%. The Conservative's framing — current ratio is fine, the trajectory is not — is the correct one; the Aggressive's "+$22.1B net cash, 30x coverage, 21.4% ROE" rebuts solvency, which nobody contested, and never rebuts direction of travel. The Conservative's mark-to-model point also stands unanswered: ~31% of Q1 net income came from private-AI-stake revaluations, a two-sided mark that can produce an optical EPS miss while the operating story is intact — precisely the kind of item that gaps rather than drifts.

Technicals break for the bear on method as well as direction. The Aggressive's June 25 precedent is real but non-transferable, and the Neutral's rebuttal is decisive: that move ran from ~227 to 254.96 and was fully retraced, and every condition that produced it is absent now. Five consecutive lower closes, a close at 226.65 (lowest since 2026-04-08 at 221.25), price below the 10 EMA (236.46), 50 SMA (246.97), 200 SMA (234.66), VWMA (242.21) and the lower Bollinger band (227.45); MACD −3.751 with the histogram expanding five straight sessions (−0.297 → −1.986); distribution volume of 47.47M/44.52M/44.96M on the down days versus 27.7–34.6M on quiet advances, with 44.96M on 07-29 against a ~39.1M 20-session average; and no confirmed bullish divergence (RSI 33.31 now versus 33.63 at the 06-25 low, with price lower). The rising 200 SMA is the most backward-looking line on the page and will keep rising mechanically while price falls. The risk/reward is also mispriced at both ends: the downside does not stop at 225.55 — it runs 221.25 → 219.62 → 213.77 → 209.77 — while the upside must claw through seven stacked layers (230.86–232.82, 234.66, 236.46, 238.35, 242.21/242.72, 246.97, 249.89–254.96). And the event is genuinely binary and symmetric: there are no Q2 2026 results, no guidance detail, and no AMZN-issued news in the sample, so "fear is already priced" is fabrication, not a positioning read — the only stock-specific price fact in the news is that AMZN "dipped."

Why Underweight and not Sell.
